summary:
Every visitor to West Virginia stands first under the federal travel-document regime. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary, barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their gender identity, and prohibited self-selection of gender on passports and visas. The State Department stopped processing the X marker and any marker not matching sex assigned at birth; new passport applications are processed only as M or F according to supporting documents, and passports already issued with an X marker remain valid until they expire. The Supreme Court in November 2025 allowed the passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect, superseding a State Department policy in place since 1992. A trans or nonbinary visitor can therefore arrive holding papers that do not match their presentation, with airport screening and visa decisions following the same national rules, including the February 2025 State Department policy refusing visas to trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sporting events and treating applicants who list a gender other than their assigned sex as grounds for a permanent ban for fraud.

West Virginia's own facility restriction is statutory. Governor Patrick Morrisey signed Senate Bill 456, the 'Riley Gaines Act,' on 12 March 2025, after the state Senate passed it on 3 March and the House of Delegates passed it on 6 March. The statute defines 'woman' as an adult human of the female sex and 'man' as an adult human of the male sex and aims to preserve women's single-sex spaces, covering locker rooms, bathrooms, rape crisis centers, dormitories, prisons, and domestic violence shelters. At the signing, Morrisey said bathrooms, locker rooms, domestic violence shelters and rape crisis centers 'should be kept private for women only.' The Movement Advancement Project equality map cataloguing state bans on transgender people's use of public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity is the source for West Virginia's facility-ban enumeration.

National risk gradings place West Virginia near the top of the risk scale. The July 2026 Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map (Erin In The Morning, published 27 August 2026) places West Virginia in 'The Worst States' group (AL, AR, IA, IN, LA, MS, OH, OK, ND, SC, SD, TN, UT, WV, WY), one tier below 'Do Not Travel' (FL, ID, KS, TX), within a national frame of 'Worst Policies In Effect'. Idaho was promoted to 'Do Not Travel' as the fourth such state after its felony bathroom ban, which carries up to 5 years and is partially court-blocked but in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists.
tangentialFactors:
West Virginia's facility statute is part of a wider national pattern. A Movement Advancement Project tally counts state bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings in nine states and one territory, with outright state bans on facility use per gender identity in additional states; 29 states, four territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban, and some states make trans bathroom use a criminal offence in certain circumstances. Idaho's felony bathroom ban carries up to 5 years and is partially court-blocked but in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists.

Several federal measures affecting trans visitors have been blocked or enjoined in court, and the ACLU has sued the State Department over passport sex-marker restrictions on behalf of seven plaintiffs. Multiple foreign governments have responded to US identity-document and data rules: in April 2025 CNN reported that several countries issued advisories about trans people travelling to the United States, and Axios reported in March 2025 that at least eight European countries, including Finland and Denmark, adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the US.
localsOnly:
West Virginia residents face the same statutory facility restrictions as visitors, with Senate Bill 456 reaching locker rooms, bathrooms, rape crisis centers, dormitories, prisons, and domestic violence shelters statewide. The state's birth certificate and driver's licence marker rules are not separately sourced in this inventory and are not stated here.

Residents also stand under the federal care restrictions: Executive Order 14187 (January 2025) described gender-affirming care for minors as 'chemical and surgical mutilation of children,' leading some hospitals to pause care; in summer 2025 the Department of Justice subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for full records of patients under 19. In July 2025 the federal government shut down specialised LGBTQ youth services on the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, and October 2025 proposed rules would bar Medicaid reimbursement for care to transgender patients under 18. Gender-affirming care for children is already banned in 27 states.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Movement Advancement Project equality map URL cited for West Virginia's facility-ban enumeration now returns a 404 because MAP has moved the page; the underlying tally is reported as the source but the live page could not be retrieved in this pass.

West Virginia's specific birth-certificate and driver's licence gender-marker rules are not covered by this source inventory and remain unresolved here. Whether West Virginia has been separately flagged beyond the 'The Worst States' tier, or has pending legislation mirroring Kansas's February 2026 document-invalidating statute, is not sourced in this inventory.
